sources.ref_file_title: Ale03 - More on average case vs approximation complexity
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib (FOCS:Alekhnovich03: FOCS 2003, pp. 298-307, doi 10.1109/SFCS.2003.1238204). Abstract: 'There exists a secure public-key (probabilistic) cryptosystem, based on the intractability of decoding of random binary codes.' Alekhnovich's conjecture concerns decoding random binary codes at noise weight ~sqrt(n); the decisional LPN(eps = Theta(1/sqrt(k))) reading is the standard modern restatement (e.g. BBBS16 'On Public Key Encryption from Noisy Codewords', YZ16).

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction that uses LPN samples only as data: public key and ciphertexts are noisy codewords of a public random code. The security proof is two straight-line hybrids (public key to uniform, then ciphertext to uniform), each a fixed reduction that runs any IND-CPA distinguisher once, as an oracle, to distinguish LPN samples from uniform. One fixed construction, one fixed reduction, adversary used only as an oracle: the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.model_justification: Plain-model construction; no idealized oracle or setup.
pages.statement: Hardness of decisional [[learning-parity-with-noise#noise-level|mid-noise LPN]] at noise rate $\varepsilon = \Theta(1/\sqrt{k})$, the $\gamma = 1/2$ point of the $\varepsilon = 1/k^{\gamma}$ family, implies IND-CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]] — [[Ale03 - More on average case vs approximation complexity|Ale03]]. Hardness at any lower noise rate, in particular the low-noise regime $\varepsilon = \log^{c}(k)/k$, implies hardness at $\Theta(1/\sqrt{k})$ by adding independent noise ([[noise-level-to-noise-level|noise monotonicity]]), so the same conclusion follows.
pages.sketch: Public keys and ciphertexts are noisy codewords of a public random linear code (equivalently, their syndromes) with noise vectors of weight $\Theta(\sqrt{m})$; the secret key is the public key's noise vector $\mathbf{e}$. By duality the receiver obtains $\langle \mathbf{e}, \tilde{\mathbf{e}} \rangle + \beta$ from a ciphertext with noise $\tilde{\mathbf{e}}$ encrypting the bit $\beta$; two independent weight-$\Theta(\sqrt{m})$ vectors in $\FF_2^m$ overlap in $O(1)$ positions in expectation, so the inner product is biased toward $0$ and $\beta$ is recovered with constant advantage, which standard amplification boosts. Security is two decisional-LPN hybrids, replacing the public key and then the ciphertext by uniform strings.
flags: Hypothesis id lpn-mid-noise covers the whole eps = 1/k^gamma family (gamma < 1); Ale03 needs only the gamma = 1/2 instance. The literature calls this regime 'low-noise LPN', which collides with this wiki's stricter 'low-noise' (log^c(k)/k) label — the statement pins the concrete rate.

Duplicate edge: content/Reductions/lpn-to-pke.md (red-lpn-to-pke, batch red-18) records the same claim with flat hypothesis lpn and no citation; merge with this page (regime-qualified hypothesis, citation) as the survivor. The red-18 verified entry proposes the same merge.

sources.ref_file_title: LMW23 - Doubly Efficient Private Information Retrieval and Fully Homomorphic RAM Computation from Ring LWE
sources.authors: Wei-Kai Lin, Ethan Mook, Daniel Wichs
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib (STOC:LinMooWic23: STOC 2023, pp. 595-608, doi 10.1145/3564246.3585175); eprint 2022/1703 is the wiki page's source. Abstract: unkeyed DEPIR with deterministic preprocessing, secure under standard RingLWE; preprocessing time/size O(N^{1+eps}), per-query time and communication polylog(N), updates in O(N^eps); built by first constructing a PIR whose server computation is multivariate polynomial evaluation, then preprocessing the polynomial with Kedlaya-Umans.

pages.class_justification: LMW23 do not classify the reduction, and the conclusion carries an efficiency requirement (sublinear server time after preprocessing) outside the RTV04 security-only axes. Left unstated.
pages.model_justification: Plain model; the preprocessing is deterministic and public, with no random oracle or common setup.
pages.statement: Hardness of [[learning-with-errors#ring-lwe|Ring-LWE]] implies unkeyed [[doubly-efficient-pir|DEPIR]]: for every constant $\varepsilon > 0$, the server deterministically preprocesses a database of size $N$ in time and space $O(N^{1+\varepsilon})$, after which each query costs $\polylog(N)$ server time and communication, and updates cost $O(N^{\varepsilon})$ — [[LMW23 - Doubly Efficient Private Information Retrieval and Fully Homomorphic RAM Computation from Ring LWE|LMW23]].
pages.sketch: LMW23 first build a PIR whose server computation is evaluating a fixed multivariate polynomial: the database is encoded as a low-degree polynomial, the query is a Ring-LWE somewhat-homomorphic encryption of the index point, and homomorphic evaluation is literal polynomial evaluation over the ciphertext ring. Preprocessing that polynomial with the Kedlaya–Umans data structure for fast multipoint evaluation makes each online evaluation polylogarithmic.
notes_to_keep: LMW23 also construct RAM-FHE from Ring-LWE with circular security — a second conclusion with no object page of its own.
flags: Frontmatter hypothesis should be ring-lwe, not lwe: LMW23 prove security under RingLWE specifically (title and abstract), and the LWE page defines ring-lwe as a variant id.

The migrated bullet writes the storage bound in N and the online bound in n, and states the online cost as O(log^{1/eps}(n)); the abstract states polylog(N) — the statement follows the abstract and uses N throughout.

sources.ref_file_title: LMW24 - Doubly Efficient Cryptography Commitments, Arguments and RAM MPC
sources.authors: Wei-Kai Lin, Ethan Mook, Daniel Wichs
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib (C:LinMooWic24: CRYPTO 2024 Part VIII, pp. 240-273) and the Springer DOI via WebSearch; the wiki page's source eprint 2025/235 is the paper's 2025 major-revision posting. Abstract: doubly efficient commitments, doubly succinct arguments, commit-prove-and-locally-open, and RAM-MPC with malicious security, all in the plain model without common setup; parties preprocess inputs offline then run many executions in sublinear online time; DEPIR is the building block; instantiated from Ring LWE.

pages.class_justification: LMW24 do not classify the reduction, and the conclusion bundles efficiency (sublinear online time) with security, outside the RTV04 axes. Left unstated.
pages.model_justification: Plain model, explicitly without any common setup.
pages.statement: Hardness of [[learning-with-errors#ring-lwe|Ring-LWE]] implies maliciously secure [[doubly-efficient-ram-mpc|doubly efficient RAM-MPC]] in the plain model: each party preprocesses its input once, offline, and then runs arbitrarily many executions with arbitrary other parties in online time proportional to the RAM running time of the program, which may be sublinear in the input size — [[LMW24 - Doubly Efficient Cryptography Commitments, Arguments and RAM MPC|LMW24]]. The same work gives doubly efficient commitments and doubly succinct arguments whose committer and prover run in sublinear online time.
pages.sketch: DEPIR, instantiated from Ring-LWE via LMW23, yields doubly efficient commitments whose sender preprocesses its input and later commits and opens individual bits in sublinear time; these give doubly succinct interactive arguments and a commit-prove-and-locally-open protocol, from which the RAM-MPC is assembled.
flags: Frontmatter hypothesis should be ring-lwe, not lwe: LMW24's constructions are instantiated from Ring LWE (via the LMW23 DEPIR); the abstract names no plain-LWE instantiation.

The edge factors through DEPIR: LMW24 explicitly build on DEPIR as the main building block, so a cleaner split is ring-lwe => depir (red-lwe-to-depir-lmw23) plus a depir => de-ram-mpc edge citing LMW24; the current page compresses the chain.

sources.ref_file_title: Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib (STOC:Regev05, pp. 84-93, doi 10.1145/1060590.1060603). Reg05 gives the IND-CPA bit-encryption scheme; a KEM that encrypts a random session key with it is the standard PKE-to-KEM step.

pages.class_justification: Composition of Regev's fixed construction with the generic PKE-to-KEM step (encrypt a random session key bit by bit). The security reduction runs the KEM adversary once, as an oracle, to break IND-CPA of the bitwise encryption and hence, through Regev's reduction, decision LWE — the fully-black-box shape, preserved under composition.
pages.model_justification: Regev's scheme and the PKE-to-KEM step need no idealized oracle. (The FO transform in the migrated Kyber quote is a ROM result on a different edge.)
pages.statement: Hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] implies an [[key-encapsulation-mechanism#ind-cpa-kem|IND-CPA KEM]]: encapsulation samples a uniformly random session key and encrypts it bit by bit under Regev's LWE encryption scheme — [[Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography|Reg05]].
pages.sketch: A distinguisher between the encapsulated key and an independent random key is an IND-CPA adversary against the bitwise Regev encryption of the key, hence, by a hybrid over the key bits, a decision-LWE distinguisher.

sources.ref_file_title: GSW13 - Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based
sources.authors: Craig Gentry, Amit Sahai, Brent Waters
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib (C:GenSahWat13: CRYPTO 2013 Part I, LNCS 8042, pp. 75-92); also eprint 2013/340; Springer DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-40041-4_5. Abstract (via WebSearch snippet): approximate-eigenvector method; homomorphic addition and multiplication are matrix addition and multiplication; no relinearization; no evaluation key. Same ref_file_title as the red-04 verified entry that also proposes GSW13.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction. The public key is an acyclic chain of key-switching hints (LWE encryptions of level-$j$ key material under the level-$(j-1)$ key), so the security proof is a hybrid over levels in which each step converts the IND-CPA adversary, used only as an oracle, into a decision-LWE distinguisher: the fully-black-box shape.
pages.model_justification: Plain-model construction; the point of the leveled scheme is that it needs neither bootstrapping nor a circular-security assumption.
pages.statement: For every depth bound $L$ fixed at key generation, hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] with modulus-to-noise ratio growing with $L$ yields [[homomorphic-encryption#leveled-fully-homomorphic-encryption|leveled FHE]] for all polynomial-size circuits of depth $L$, without bootstrapping and without a circular-security assumption — [[BGV12 - Leveled fully homomorphic encryption without bootstrapping|BGV12]].
pages.sketch: Ciphertexts are Regev-style LWE encryptions under a ladder of moduli $q_L > \cdots > q_0$. After each multiplication, key switching returns the ciphertext from the tensored secret to a fresh secret, and modulus switching rescales it from $q_j$ to $q_{j-1}$, dividing the noise by the same factor; the noise magnitude therefore stays at $B$ while the modulus shrinks one rung per level, so depth $L$ is reached without bootstrapping.
pages.improvements_text: - The approximate-eigenvector method gives leveled FHE from LWE with no evaluation key and no relinearization: homomorphic addition and multiplication are matrix addition and multiplication — [[GSW13 - Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based|GSW13]]
flags: BGV12 also give a Ring-LWE instantiation with better efficiency; the plain-LWE hypothesis recorded here is correct for the main theorem.

BV11 (Brakerski-Vaikuntanathan, FOCS 2011; proposed as a new reference by batch red-04) built FHE from standard LWE first, with bootstrapping; BGV12's contribution is leveled FHE without bootstrapping. The migrated 'first efficient construction from LWE' gloss is not preserved.

Verifier could not read BGV12 or GSW13 (eprint/Springer/ACM egress-blocked); bibliographic data verified offline via vendor/cryptobib, the GSW13 abstract claims via WebSearch snippets, and the BGV noise/modulus behaviour via snippets of follow-up work.

improvements_text: 'no key or modulus switching' -> 'no evaluation key and no relinearization', the claims the GSW13 abstract makes
statement tightened to one sentence; class_justification tightened

sources.ref_file_title: Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib (STOC:Regev05, pp. 84-93, doi 10.1145/1060590.1060603). Journal version: J. ACM 56(6), 2009.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction using only samples of the LWE distribution; the security proof runs any IND-CPA adversary once, as an oracle, inside a two-step hybrid: decision LWE replaces the public key by uniform, after which the leftover hash lemma makes the challenge ciphertext statistically independent of the bit. Any advantage difference is a decision-LWE distinguisher.
pages.model_justification: Plain-model construction. (Reg05's separate worst-case hardness theorem for LWE is a quantum reduction, but that is a different edge: red-gapsvp-to-lwe-reg05 / red-sivp-to-lwe-reg05.)
pages.statement: Hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] with $m = O(n \log q)$ samples implies IND-CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]]: the public key is $m$ LWE samples, and a bit $\mu$ is encrypted as a random subset-sum of them plus $\mu \lfloor q/2 \rfloor$ — [[Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography|Reg05]].
pages.sketch: $\KeyGen$ outputs $\pk = (\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{s} + \mathbf{e})$ and $\sk = \mathbf{s}$; $\Enc(\pk, \mu)$ samples $\mathbf{r} \getsr \bits^m$ and outputs $(\mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{A},\ \mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{b} + \mu \lfloor q/2 \rfloor)$; $\Dec(\sk, (\mathbf{c}_1, c_2))$ computes $c_2 - \langle \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{s} \rangle = \mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{e} + \mu \lfloor q/2 \rfloor$ and rounds. Security: decision LWE replaces $(\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{b})$ by uniform, after which $(\mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{b})$ is statistically close to uniform by the leftover hash lemma, so the ciphertext hides $\mu$.
flags: The migrated key-exchange bullet (KE from LWE 'as a special case of PKE from LWE') is the composite lwe => pke => ke; the second link is the existing red-pke-to-ke page and should not be re-recorded here.
The 'security rooted in worst-case lattice hardness' clause is the separate worst-case edge (red-gapsvp-to-lwe-reg05 / red-sivp-to-lwe-reg05), already recorded.
verifier_changes: statement and sketch lightly tightened (no content change); cryptobib verification recorded in the source note

sources.ref_file_title: DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications
sources.authors: Nico Döttling, Sanjam Garg, Yuval Ishai, Giulio Malavolta, Tamer Mour, Rafail Ostrovsky
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib (C:DGIMMO19: CRYPTO 2019 Part III, pp. 3-32); eprint 2019/639 is the wiki page's source. Abstract: 'We obtain constructions where the hint is only one bit long based on DDH, QR, DCR, or LWE.'

pages.class_justification: DGI+19 do not classify the reduction. Index hiding is a single hybrid that replaces the encoding key by uniform under decision LWE, running the adversary as an oracle, but the source does not state a class and the verifier could not check the paper's security definition for TDH in full — left unstated.
pages.statement: Hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] implies [[trapdoor-hash-function|TDH]] with one-bit hints: for every index $i$ one samples an encoding key hiding $i$ together with a trapdoor that recovers the input bit $x_i$ from the hash $H(x)$ and a single hint bit — [[DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications|DGI+19]].
pages.sketch: The hash of $x \in \bits^m$ is $\mathbf{A}x$ for a public $\mathbf{A} \in \ZZ_q^{n \times m}$; the encoding key for index $i$ is an LWE encryption $\mathbf{s}^{\top}\mathbf{A} + \mathbf{e}^{\top} + \lfloor q/2 \rfloor \mathbf{u}_i^{\top}$ of the $i$-th unit vector, and the hint is $\langle \mathrm{ek}, x \rangle$ rounded to one bit. The trapdoor $\mathbf{s}$ and $H(x) = \mathbf{A}x$ give $\mathbf{s}^{\top}\mathbf{A}x$, so the decoder outputs the two candidate hints for $x_i = 0$ and $x_i = 1$ and the receiver keeps the one that matches, which is correct unless the small error $\mathbf{e}^{\top}x$ crosses a rounding boundary; index hiding is exactly LWE pseudorandomness of the encoding key.
notes_to_keep: The sub-bullet's claim that TDH generically yields PIR is an independent edge (TDH ⇒ PIR, DGI+19) that is not yet recorded.
flags: DGI+19 also construct TDH from DDH, QR, and DCR. Sibling edges exist for DDH (red-ddh-to-tdh-dgi-19) and QR (red-qr-to-tdh-dgi-19); a dcr-to-tdh-dgi-19 edge is missing.
The migrated quote records only the PIR application; the DGI+19 TDH => PIR link deserves its own reduction page (distinct from the existing red-tdh-to-cpir-amr25, which cites AMR25).
